raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a single-panel line plot illustrating how “Coverage” varies with the “Number of completions (k)” for four model conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (k)” and uses a logarithmic base-2 scale with tick labels at \(2^0, 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^5, 2^6, 2^7, 2^8\) (from 1 to 256). The y-axis is labeled “Coverage” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from about 0.2 up to just under 1.0, with visible gridlines and labeled ticks around 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. There are four data series with a legend inside the plot: (1) “Llama-3B” shown as a blue solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 0.43 at \(2^0\) to about 0.92 at \(2^8\); (2) “Llama-3B + FT” shown as a green dotted line with triangular markers, rising from about 0.44 at \(2^0\) to about 0.91 at \(2^8\); (3) “Llama-1B” shown as a light blue solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 0.25 at \(2^0\) to about 0.88 at \(2^8\); and (4) “Llama-1B + FT” shown as a light green dotted line with triangular markers, increasing from about 0.26 at \(2^0\) to about 0.86 at \(2^8\). All four lines show a monotonic upward trend across k, with the steepest increases occurring at lower k and more gradual increases toward higher k.
